headline: Israel issues NEW displacement orders for 10+ south Lebanon towns, several north of the Litani
dek: Israel's military issued new forced displacement orders covering more than 10 villages/towns in southern Lebanon, including several in Nabatieh district north of the Litani River; residents told to evacuate immediately at least 1,000 metres into open areas. Three of the towns are receiving such…
sources: IDF Arabic-language spokesman Avichay Adraee post on X, reported by Al Jazeera; Netanyahu statement via Al Jazeera newsfeed
fault_line: Ceasefire on paper vs expansion on the ground: is Israel's area of operations in Lebanon still growing north of the Litani?

sections.what_happened: Israel's military issued new forced displacement orders covering more than 10 villages/towns in southern Lebanon, including several in Nabatieh district north of the Litani River; residents told to evacuate immediately at least 1,000 metres into open areas. Three of the towns are receiving such orders for the first time (AJ Beirut correspondent Rory Challands). Lebanon's NNA later reported strikes across the south including towns not in the order. Separately Netanyahu said a ceasefire is not in effect in Lebanon ('We are continuing to strike Hezbollah with force') while offering 'peace negotiations' at Lebanon's request. Lebanon Health Ministry: at least 10 killed Saturday; total since Mar 2 escalation 2,659 killed, 8,183 injured.
sections.what_verified: IDF spokesman primary post; AJ reporting/correspondent; Lebanon NNA; Lebanon Ministry of Public Health toll.
sections.what_disputed: US-brokered ceasefire announced Apr 17, extended to May 17, is the standing framework; President Aoun said Israel should fully implement the ceasefire before direct talks. AJ's Challands: the ceasefire 'exists only in name'. Israel's stated target is Hezbollah; AJ notes a large proportion of those killed have been civilians. Earlier Nov 1 triages of Lebanon displacement orders were a May recirculation — distinct from this new order set.
sections.why_matters: 'No ceasefire' in his own words + 10+ towns told to leave, some for the first time, north of the Litani — the map is moving while the truce is still on paper. Hard number: 2,659 killed since Mar 2.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (AJ article published 00:03Z Nov 2; surfaced in-window) -- Israel issues NEW displacement orders for 10+ south Lebanon towns, several north of the Litani; Netanyahu: 'no ceasefire in Lebanon'

totw_analysis: Our read: 'No ceasefire' in his own words + 10+ towns told to leave, some for the first time, north of the Litani — the map is moving while the truce is still on paper. Hard number: 2,659 killed since Mar 2. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Ceasefire on paper vs expansion on the ground: is Israel's area of operations in Lebanon still growing north of the Litani?
